texts.label: D'Orvilliers to the Navy minister, Cayenne, 10 June 1761 (C14 25 fol. 36), reading by Brice Dudout
texts.summary: In the middle of the Seven Years’ War, cut off from France, the governor of French Guiana writes to the minister a letter almost entirely in cipher. He backs Captain Des Essarts’s plan: to bring from Holland, through Rotterdam and Surinam, “goods for sugar works” that will in fact clothe a garrison in rags; then he admits that a breach of twelve toises has opened in the royal bastion and that he has not a sou to repair it. The colonial office deciphered another copy (“the triplicate deciphered”); this one was never translated, and the ANOM inventory still calls it “entirely in cipher and not translated”.
